After passing through the mechanical screen, raw wastewater flows into a packaged grit chamber (i.e., a cyclone grit removal type system).

The activated sludge treatment system consists of two contact stabilization tanks (CSTs). Air from centrifugal blowers is delivered to the activated sludge by air diffusers installed on the floor of the contact tank, re-aeration tank, and digester.
The CSTs process is characterized as an activated sludge process...clarification (clarifier)
The circular tanks are compartmented ... and sludge digestion (digester). Air from centrifugal blowers is delivered ... to the ... digester.
Sludge removed from the CSTs digester is conveyed via sludge wasting pumps which pump the sludge to the drying beds on the south end of the plant.

The OD process is characterized as a modified extended aeration activated sludge process with a relatively long sludge age...include a large aeration basin and a relatively smaller anoxic zone for denitrification.
The two circular clarifiers settle and collect sludge.
The settled sludge is pulled from the bottom of the clarifier and continuously pumped back into the OD to maintain the mixed liquor concentration.

The clarified effluent from the CSTs and OD processes is disinfected using an automated chlorine delivery system... The chlorinated effluent travels through the serpentine contact chamber and overtops a weir where sodium bisulfite is added to remove any remaining residual chlorine.

Solids are dried through a combination of evaporation and draw-off or decant of supernatant, which is returned to the Facility’s headworks.
